ROOFTOP RIVALS

Move list

Every attack has startup, an active window, and recovery. Hold away from your opponent to guard. Block crouching kicks low and jumping attacks high.

Movement

W A S D or arrows

Up: jump · Down: crouch
Back: high guard · Down + back: low guard

Six-button attacks

J K L Punch
U I O Kick

Left to right: light, medium, heavy.

Ken / Ryu — facing right

HadokenOne projectile at a time.
↓ ↘ → + PunchShortcut: Q · medium strength
ShoryukenInvulnerable start; punishable landing.
→ ↓ ↘ + PunchShortcut: E · medium strength
TatsumakiAlso usable in the air.
↓ ↙ ← + KickShortcut: R · medium strength
Shoulder throw / back rollUnblockable, point-blank range.
← or → + MP / HP / MK / HKPunch throws; kick rolls. Direction chooses the side.

Reverse motions when facing left. Punch or kick strength changes speed, damage, reach, and recovery. Connect a normal, then quickly enter a special to cancel its recovery. Jumping attacks can link into grounded combos.

Gamepad

Standard controller: D-pad or left stick to move. X / Y / RB are light / medium / heavy punches; A / B / RT are light / medium / heavy kicks. Start pauses. PlayStation equivalents: Square / Triangle / R1, Cross / Circle / R2. Motion inputs work on the directional pad.

Touch

Slide the eight-way pad for motions or hold diagonals. Six separate buttons preserve all strengths. Optional HADO / SHORYU / TATSU buttons perform medium specials. Landscape gives the arena more breathing room.

Repeated hits can cause a dizzy state; tap directions and attacks to recover faster. Sweeps and throws knock down. Knock a rival into an edge sign to break it. Win two rounds to finish the duel. Escape / P pauses; Enter starts or rematches.

Rooftop Rivals: Turbo Duel is an unofficial, non-commercial vertical slice inspired by Street Fighter II Turbo for Super NES. Play Ken or Ryu in one complete rooftop matchup, from opening bell to results.

Launch

Open this HTML directly in a modern browser. No server, installation, ROM, external asset, or network is needed. Click Start Match to enable audio. Settings and records save locally when browser storage is available. Physical gamepad access depends on browser support.

Characters and Street Fighter names belong to Capcom. The procedural art, synthesized soundtrack, interface, and adaptation-specific rules were created for this demo. This is not a ROM, emulator, official release, or frame-exact reconstruction.
